question: Is the focused handler, workflow-source, Crabbox, and green-check evidence sufficient to merge under a monitored natural-failure canary, or must this remain unmerged until staging/shadow proof exists?
rationale: The deployed recovery path cannot be observed before merge without manually dispatching, rerunning, cancelling, or inducing a control-plane failure, so automation cannot choose the acceptable proof threshold or own the rollback risk.

options.title: Approve monitored canary
options.body: Merge only with an explicitly owned rollback boundary, then use the first naturally occurring failed shard to verify one acknowledgement, no direct fanout, preserved live work, skipped verdict routing, non-actionable comments, and bounded termination.

options.title: Hold for shadow proof
options.body: Keep the PR in draft until a safe staging or shadow environment can exercise the deployed Worker and GitHub Actions recovery path without manufacturing production failure.

recommendation.title: Approve monitored canary
recommendation.body: Merge only with an explicitly owned rollback boundary, then use the first naturally occurring failed shard to verify one acknowledgement, no direct fanout, preserved live work, skipped verdict routing, non-actionable comments, and bounded termination.

likelyOwner.reason: Their current-main history most directly owns the exact-review queue, alarm recovery, target capacity, and bounded fanout behavior affected by the rollout decision.
